chunks: Yunus, from Abu Sabit and Ibn Awn, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding

a man who had a right upon another man, so he lost him and did not know where to seek him, and did not know if he was alive or dead, and did not know of an inheritor for him, nor a clan, nor a city. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Seek him.' He said, 'If that is prolonged, should I give it in charity?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Seek him.'

key_terms.أَتَصَدَّقُ بِهِ: should I give in charity with it
key_terms.حَيٌّ هُوَ أَمْ مَيِّتٌ: whether he is alive or dead

ai.seo_question: What should a creditor do if the debtor is lost and unknown?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of *istidlal* (presumption of existence) for the debtor, prioritizing the fulfillment of the specific debt obligation over the general merit of charity. It reflects the Shia juristic view that a debt is a concrete right (*haqq*) attached to the individual, which cannot be extinguished merely by the creditor's inability to locate them, thereby requiring persistent effort to ensure justice is served.
